question.text: An investor submits a mutual fund application through a distributor without specifying whether the application is for the Direct Plan or the Regular Plan. How is the application processed?

answer.text: The application is rejected for being incomplete
The investment is considered to be in the Regular Plan, because the application is routed through a distributor
The investment is routed to the Direct Plan by default
The AMC contacts the investor to clarify before processing

explanation.text: The Logic: Where an investor's mutual fund application is routed through a distributor (i.e., an ARN-holder's code appears on the form), it is treated as a Regular Plan investment. Where required selections beyond the scheme name (plan, option, pay-out option) are not specified, the default printed in the scheme's application-form instructions applies. The mode of submission — through a distributor versus directly with the AMC — therefore determines whether the application is processed under the Regular Plan. The Trap: The form is not rejected merely because the plan box is unticked, since the default-options mechanism resolves the omission. The application is also not routed to the Direct Plan by default when a distributor's ARN is present, and AMCs do not pause processing to call the investor where defaults can be applied. Note: The Series V-A (Mutual Fund Distributors) workbook states that an investment routed through a distributor is considered a Regular Plan investment and that unspecified selections follow the default option printed in the application-form instructions. The wider claim that the Direct Plan is the universal default is general industry framing and is not supported on the cited pages of this workbook.
